headline: Windows 11 Media Player uses 3.5x more RAM, paywalls codecs
summary: Microsoft's new Media Player for Windows 11 is reportedly using significantly more memory than its predecessor and is now charging for popular video codecs.
details: Microsoft's latest Media Player for Windows 11 is facing criticism for its performance and feature limitations. Tests indicate the new player consumes approximately 377MB of RAM when idle, a stark contrast to the classic Windows Media Player's 103MB usage—about 3.5 times more memory.

Beyond the increased memory footprint, the new player also exhibits slower startup times for local video files, with load times increasing by roughly 50%. This performance dip is a notable regression from the legacy player.

The controversy extends to codec support, as Microsoft now requires users to purchase the "HEVC Video Extensions" app from the Microsoft Store for HEVC (H.265) playback. This move effectively paywalls a popular video format.

Furthermore, Microsoft has confirmed that Windows 11 version 24H2 will remove the built-in AC‑3 (Dolby Digital) codec. This means the new Media Player on these systems will not natively support AC‑3 audio tracks, potentially impacting playback of many media files.

The new Media Player is intended to replace both Groove Music and the classic Windows Media Player as the default on Windows 11. While the classic player remains available as an optional component, Microsoft is clearly pushing users towards its newer, more resource-intensive software.
For users seeking a more robust and less restrictive media playback experience, third-party players like VLC offer built-in codec support and do not rely on paid add-ons from Microsoft.
